matched.expectedTitle: IDS Rate Limit Evasion via X-Forwarded-For Spoofing
matched.actualTitle: Spam Prevention Bypass - No Rate Limiting Implemented
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify rate limiting bypass vulnerabilities. While the actual finding focuses on /api/feedback endpoint lacking rate limits and the expected finding targets IDS rate limiting via X-Forwarded-For spoofing, they represent the same vulnerability category: attackers can bypass rate limiting to send unlimited requests. The actual finding demonstrates rate limiting is completely absent, which achieves the same evasion outcome as X-Forwarded-For spoofing.

matched.expectedTitle: Blind SQL Injection in Product Search
matched.actualTitle: SQL Injection - Data Extraction via Products Search
matched.matchReason: Direct match. Both findings identify SQL injection via the category parameter in /api/products endpoint. The actual finding provides detailed proof of boolean-based blind SQLi and data extraction capabilities. The expected finding describes the same vulnerability in the same file with identical attack vectors and impact.

matched.expectedTitle: CRLF Log Injection in User-Agent Header
matched.actualTitle: Stored XSS via WAF Filter Bypass in Feedback Endpoint
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify stored injection vulnerabilities that bypass WAF filters. While the expected finding focuses on CRLF injection in logs and the actual finding shows stored XSS via encoding bypass, they represent the same category of vulnerability: stored injection attacks that evade WAF detection and allow log/data poisoning. Both demonstrate how WAF filters can be bypassed through encoding techniques.

matched.actualTitle: SQL Injection in /api/feedback Endpoint with WAF Bypass
matched.matchReason: Both findings demonstrate WAF bypass techniques. The actual finding proves WAF bypass using comment insertion (/**/) and keyword splitting (UNI/**/ON) to inject SQL into /api/feedback endpoint. The expected finding describes WAF bypass via chunked Transfer-Encoding. Both show incomplete WAF rule implementation that can be circumvented through payload obfuscation.

matched.actualTitle: Incomplete WAF Protection - SQL Injection Bypass via Comment Syntax
matched.matchReason: Both findings identify protocol/rule-level bypasses that allow attackers to circumvent security controls. The expected finding shows HTTP/1.0 protocol bypass of IDS inspection, while the actual finding demonstrates comment syntax bypass of WAF filters. Both represent incomplete security implementation that allows bypassing inspection rules through protocol or syntax variations. The core vulnerability is the same: incomplete rule coverage allowing protocol/syntax-based evasion.

matched.expectedTitle: Combined Defense Evasion Chain to Flag
matched.actualTitle: SQL Injection in Admin Login Endpoint - Authentication Bypass
matched.matchReason: Both findings describe chains of vulnerabilities that enable complete system compromise. The expected finding describes combining multiple evasion techniques (X-Forwarded-For spoofing, blind SQLi, CRLF injection, WAF bypass, HTTP/1.0 bypass) to access the flag endpoint. The actual findings document the individual vulnerabilities in the chain: SQL injection in admin login allows authentication bypass, multiple SQL injections in products/feedback endpoints, WAF bypasses, and rate limiting evasion. Together, these actual findings represent the same attack chain described in the expected finding, all leading to unauthorized access to protected admin functionality.

extra.title: Health Endpoint Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Exposes service name and framework details (Express.js) without authentication or rate limiting. Enables reconnaissance and fingerprinting attacks. Not specifically mentioned in expected findings but represents valid information disclosure vulnerability.

extra.title: Missing Required Parameter Validation - Input Validation Bypass
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Missing validation for required parameters (message and rating) allowing submission of empty/null values and invalid defaults. Enables spam, duplicate entries, and metrics corruption. Not explicitly described in expected findings but represents a distinct input validation vulnerability.

extra.title: Feedback Rating Input Validation Bypass - Negative Ratings Accepted
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Rating parameter accepts out-of-range values (negative numbers, zero, extreme values) without validation. Enables reputation manipulation and metrics corruption. Related to but distinct from parameter validation bypass.

extra.title: Replay Attack / Idempotency Bypass Vulnerability
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Endpoint lacks idempotency protection allowing replay attacks. Identical requests can be submitted unlimited times, creating duplicate entries and inflating metrics. Enables rating manipulation and spam attacks.

extra.title: Unauthorized Access to WAF Statistics Endpoint & Information Disclosure
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Publicly accessible statistics endpoint exposes real-time WAF metrics, rule counts, and operational intelligence without authentication. Enables attacker reconnaissance. Demonstrates differential WAF protection where admin endpoints lack WAF rules that protect user endpoints.

extra.title: WAF Information Disclosure via Unauthenticated Endpoints
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Multiple endpoints disclose WAF implementation details, engine type (ModSecurity-sim), version, rule identifiers, and API routes without authentication. Enables targeted WAF evasion research.

extra.title: WAF Rule Name Disclosure via Error Messages
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. WAF error messages leak specific rule names (SQL_INJECTION_DETECTED, SQL_INJECTION_IN_URL) and request IDs, enabling attackers to understand WAF coverage and craft targeted bypass payloads.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Unauthenticated Service Metadata Exposure
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Root endpoint exposes service name, version 1.0.0, WAF configuration, statistics, and complete API route documentation without authentication. Enables comprehensive reconnaissance.

extra.title: Information Disclosure - Admin API Documentation Exposed Without Authentication
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Admin API endpoints expose complete API documentation and structure without authentication, revealing admin endpoints and required headers. Enables reconnaissance of admin functionality.

extra.title: Differential WAF Protection - Unprotected Admin Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. WAF protection inconsistently applied. User-facing endpoints are protected while admin statistics endpoint is unprotected, allowing payloads that would be blocked elsewhere. Demonstrates incomplete security implementation.

extra.title: Docker Proxy Port 80 Misconfiguration - Service Denial
extra.assessment: New discovery - Valid security finding. Port 80 forwards to non-existent backend service causing connection resets. Service accessible on port 3058 instead. This is a configuration/infrastructure issue rather than application security vulnerability.

extra.title: Sensitive Service Information Disclosure via Root Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Duplicate/related to information disclosure findings. Root endpoint exposes comprehensive service details including DefenseMatrix name, version 1.0.0, ModSecurity-sim WAF engine, rule counts, and statistics without authentication.

extra.title: Rating Constraint Validation Bypass - Multiple Critical Business Logic Flaws
extra.assessment: New discovery - Comprehensive finding combining multiple flaws: invalid rating constraint validation, missing idempotency (replay attacks), no rate limiting, missing parameter validation, and race conditions. Effectively a synthesis of multiple distinct vulnerabilities affecting the feedback endpoint.
